failure.stage: carry the teapot upright over the mug

rounds.diagnosis: The transport subgoal put teapot.spout_tip at contact standoff above mug.opening_center (band starting at 0 cm), so every candidate goal pressed the spout and the pot's body into the mug rim and no collision-free goal existed; the pour stage inherited the same contact band, so its path and subgoal were equally jammed against the rim and could not contain a valid start either. Raising the standoff one step (contact -> small) on all three above-terms lifts the band away from the mug opening while keeping the spout centered over it, giving clearance for the pot body and for the swing during the tilt, and keeps the carry goal inside the pour stage's path band so the stages still chain.

failure.stage: carry the teapot upright over the mug
failure.message: no transport goal is a start the pour accepts

rounds.diagnosis: The standoff over the mug was too low. At the carry subgoal the spout tip sits only ~2 cm above mug.opening_center while teapot.handle_center (and hence the pot body and the gripper) is at -1.7 cm, i.e. below the mug's rim: every pose in that band puts the body/gripper into the mug, so no collision-free goal exists, and the pour stage inherits the same low band for its whole path while the pot swings 90 deg about its tilt axis. Stepping the 'above mug.opening_center' clearance from small to medium on the carry subgoal and on both the pour path and pour subgoal lifts the identical-height band farther from the rim, giving the body clearance during the hover and the tilt while keeping the spout centered over the opening; the three bands are raised together so the carry goal still lies inside the pour path region and the pour subgoal stays inside its own path.
